objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, let's continue on with this', approving RIGID-SELECTION-20261101-001's recommendation): does every law that composes like cycles keep the top layer of its selected spaces rigid? First test the non-abelian groups that compose like cycles up to order 24 and the 1020 non-simple Mal'tsev laws on three values, then attempt a proof. Find where the top-layer statement holds, whether it fails in general, and the form in which it is true. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-02: not as phrased, but in the form that matters. Every law on three values that composes like cycles is rigid; group laws keep their top rigid; in every Mal'tsev law simple abelian sections force rigid selection, so keeping emergence needs a two-layer section (at least four values). A simple five-value law containing Z4 composes like cycles and keeps knots in its top, so the global top is the wrong layer; the rigid layer is each section's top (proved for one chain ring). The knot keeps emergence on two values in its only layer. Ticket B corrected to declared domains; next: what selection leaves and how pieces glue (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when the tested families are settled by proof or exhaustive check, and the general statement is either proved, refuted by a verified counterexample, or reduced to a precisely stated open case.
title: Does every law that composes like cycles keep its top layer rigid?
